extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students of English literature, and novelists interested in literary criticism and novel craft
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting or applying E. M. Forster's seven 'universal aspects' of the novel (story, characters, plot, fantasy, prophecy, pattern, rhythm) as criteria for analysing or writing novels. The page briefly lists these aspects as defined in his 1927 lectures/book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven universal aspects of the novel identified by E. M. Forster (listed as 'story').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented by Forster as a core aspect to consider when discussing or composing novels; the book uses examples from classic texts to illustrate this aspect. (Page gives the term only; fuller exposition appears in Forster's book.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven universal aspects of the novel identified by E. M. Forster (listed as 'characters').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forster treats characters as a central dimension of the novel; the Wikipedia entry notes it as one of his defined aspects and indicates he illustrates points via classic examples. (Detailed guidance is in the original lectures/book.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven universal aspects of the novel identified by E. M. Forster (listed as 'plot').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by Forster among the universal aspects to evaluate or craft in novels; the article states Forster uses examples from classic texts to discuss such aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fantasy
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven universal aspects of the novel identified by E. M. Forster (listed as 'fantasy').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in Forster's framework as a distinct dimension of the novel; the Wikipedia page records the term as part of the seven aspects and notes Forster's use of classic-text examples to explicate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophecy
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven universal aspects of the novel identified by E. M. Forster (listed as 'prophecy').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named by Forster as a universal aspect to consider in novels; the entry gives only the label and its place within the seven-aspect list (more detail resides in Forster's book).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven universal aspects of the novel identified by E. M. Forster (listed as 'pattern').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forster includes pattern as a core aspect; the Wikipedia article notes the seven-term list and that Forster illustrates these aspects using examples from classic works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven universal aspects of the novel identified by E. M. Forster (listed as 'rhythm').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by Forster as one of the universal aspects; the Wikipedia page states these were defined in his 1927 lectures and are discussed with examples in the original book.
